originality.rationale: The exact claim concerns all nonempty sets of distinct root-attachment times: a signed harmonic-times-reciprocals factorization of every mixed interaction with final path length. Classical marginal/path-profile results do not encode insertion-age indicators. The 2026 innovation theorem is a strong broader near-match and covers first-order time decomposition, but it does not state or algebraically specify the arbitrary-order products; obtaining them requires iterated conditional-mean differences, not a mere substitution of its reported covariance table. Literature-index searches found the leaf-count analogue, not this hierarchy. Equivalent higher-order formulations remain a disclosed originality risk.
residual_risks: Higher-order root-edge Walsh coefficients could be implicit in older ancestry-indicator or insertion-history formulas not retrieved by the aliases used.

The 2026 general innovation formula may be adaptable to these mixed moments, but adapting it needs conditional higher-order dependence calculations, and no explicit complete factorization was identified.
The finite exhaustive checks independently test only n up to 8; the all-n claim relies on the analytic proof.
